messages.subject: RTMB ADREPORT( [string_vector] )
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

RTMB offers many interesting opportunities in terms of user-interface for package authors.  One opportunity I see is that the package-user could specify a character-string and then get that set of objects available during ADREPORT (e.g., for standard errors or to apply epsilon bias-correction).

I have a little mock-up below based on the `?RTMB::MakeADFun` example ... does anyone know how to do something like this?

```R
library(RTMB)
data(rivers)

# User chooses derived quantities via string-vector outside the function declaration
derived_quantities = c("logsd")

# Function is made and not changed (e.g. by package author)
f <- function(p) {
  logsd = log(p$sd)
  out = list("logsd"=logsd)
  ADREPORT( out[derived_quantities] )
  -sum(dnorm(rivers, p$mu, p$sd, log=TRUE))
}

# GOAL:  Model is run and derived quantities available in sdreport
obj <- MakeADFun(f, list(mu=0, sd=1), silent=TRUE)
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdrep = sdreport(obj)
```

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: RTMB ADREPORT( [string_vector] )
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Kasper!

In case others are interested, it appears to be even more user-friendly if you do (as shown in full below):

```R
  derived_values = mget( derived_quantities, ifnotfound=NA)
  ADREPORT( do.call("c", derived_values) )
```

Very cool!

```R

library(RTMB)
data(rivers)

# User chooses derived quantities via string-vector outside the function declaration

derived_quantities = c("logsd","logmean","does_not_exist")

# Function is made and not changed (e.g. by package author)
f <- function(p) {
  logsd = log(p$sd)

  logmean = log(p$mu)
  derived_values = mget( derived_quantities, ifnotfound=NA)
  ADREPORT( do.call("c", derived_values) )

  -sum(dnorm(rivers, p$mu, p$sd, log=TRUE))
}

# GOAL:  Model is run and derived quantities available in sdreport
obj <- MakeADFun(f, list(mu=0, sd=1), silent=TRUE)
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdrep = sdreport(obj)

summary(sdrep)
```

messages.subject: RTMB and Rcpp
messages.body_plain:
Hello all, I have a pretty general question.

I am using RTMB within a package that existed before RTMB was around. To make things faster, many package functions were written in C++ and exported to R using Rcpp.

For linear algebra, I was using RcppArmadillo and the way I have written the functions, they are not compatible with RTMB. So as a quick fix, I now just have two versions of each relevant function. One written in C++ and one written in R to be AD-compatible.

I am pretty sure that it should be possible to use C++ functions exported to R by Rcpp with RTMB, but I am not sure what I need to take care of for things to work smoothly. For example, I am pretty sure that I should use Eigen instead of Armadillo because it natively allows for AD, and after browsing the code of RTMB, I have seen that many functions are using Eigen.

I mainly want to make the C++ functions AD-compatible, just to make the package simpler to use. This is because some functions are intended to be used both inside and outside the objective function, hence C++ outside is welcome.
But just out of curiosity, I am wondering whether C++ functions would even be faster than their R counterparts, after applying MakeADFun().

Thanks in advance,
Ole

messages.subject: nbinom stuff in TMB
messages.body_plain:
Hi, folks,

   the (R)TMB versions of dnbinom() [dnbinom2 or dnbinom_robust] are not
as robust when approaching the Poisson limit as the base-R function.

   With a bit of work I could write my own adjoint code incorporating
the special cases shown below, if I needed it ...

  Or,  should the built-in TMB code be enhanced?

   Is this is an issue that affects anyone else?
   Should this be a TMB issue instead?

## demonstration code

x <- 1; mu <- 1
var_minus_mu <- 10^seq(-20, 0, length = 101)
## var = mu*(1+mu/theta) -> var_minus_mu = mu^2/theta -> theta =
mu^2/var_minus_mu
thetavec <- mu^2/var_minus_mu
varvec <- mu + var_minus_mu ## will underflow ...

fixtmb <- function(x) Im(unclass(x))
v1 <- dnbinom(x = x, mu = mu, size = thetavec, log = TRUE)
v2 <- RTMB::dnbinom2(x = x, mu = mu, var = varvec, log = TRUE) |> fixtmb()
v3 <- RTMB::dnbinom_robust(x = x, log_mu = log(mu),
                            log_var_minus_mu = log(var_minus_mu),
                            log = TRUE) |> fixtmb()

par(las = 1, bty = "l")
matplot(thetavec, cbind(v1, v2, v3), type = "l", log = "x",
         ylim = c(-2, 0), lwd = 2, col = c(1,2,4),
         ylab = "log LL")
abline(h = dpois(1, 1, log = TRUE), lty = 2)

R's version of dnbinom (dnbinom_mu, here:

https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/b130c55d9f3f018a339432a1356fd5ef79cb357e/src/nmath/dnbinom.c#L70

uses a different expression when size >> x:

  if(x == 0)/* be accurate, both for n << mu, and n >> mu :*/
	return R_D_exp(size * (size < mu ? log(size/(size+mu)) : log1p(-
mu/(size+mu))));
     if(x < 1e-10 * size) { /* don't use dbinom_raw() but MM's formula: */
	/* FIXME --- 1e-8 shows problem; rather use algdiv() from ./toms708.c */
	double p = (size < mu ? log(size/(1 + size/mu)) : log(mu / (1 + mu/size)));
	return R_D_exp(x * p - mu - lgamma1p(x) +
		       log1p(x*(x-1)/(2*size)));

messages.subject: Re: nbinom stuff in TMB
messages.body_plain:
Ben, yes definitely! This has to fixed.

The apparently not so robust dnbinom is here:
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/943a9ecf02838381c1d7094441b2880490cae53f/TMB/inst/include/tiny_ad/robust/distributions.hpp#L47
The inaccuracy is from calculating
lgamma(x + n) - lgamma(n)
for large n.
It should be reasonably easy to fix given that this code is used with forward mode AD, so branching is not an issue.

messages.subject: Re: RTMB and Rcpp
messages.body_plain:
"But just out of curiosity, I am wondering whether C++ functions would even be faster than their R counterparts, after applying MakeADFun()."

*After* applying MakeADFun the answer is no! But a C++ implementation will speed up MakeADFun.

In principle you could convert all your C++ functions to templates, that you could instantiate and export for double and AD types.
However, in terms of speed you probably won't gain much. And you might have to change the C++ code a lot.

Another way to utilize your existing C++ implementations is to write your own RTMB::ADjoint code. But that's assuming you know the derivatives.

messages.subject: sdreport S3 class in TMB
messages.body_plain:
I am working with a package that depends on TMB, i.e., FIMS, the Fisheries Integrated Modeling System, where we have S4 classes. I would like to include a slot in one of the S4 objects that is an sdreport object or an empty list. Therefore I wrote the following code to allow for an S3 class in an S4 object

methods::setOldClass(Classes = "sdreport")

I then also needed to add a new S4 class that combines sdreport and list in case the sdreport is not available. I could have chosen to combine it with NULL but I didn't.

methods::setClassUnion("sdreportOrList", members = c("sdreport", "list"))

ALL of the code works and the objects have the desired classes. Where I am running into problems is with devtools::document(). I get the following warning the first time I run devtools::document in an R session:

Warning message:
class "sdreport" is defined (with package slot 'FIMS') but no metadata object found to revise superClass information---not imported?  Making a copy in package 'FIMS'

And when I run devtools::document() again within the same R session I get

> devtools::document()
ℹ Updating FIMS documentation
ℹ Loading FIMS
Error in `load_all()`:
! Failed to load R/fimsfit.R
Caused by error in `methods::setOldClass()`:
! inconsistent old-style class information for "sdreport"; the class is defined but does not extend "oldClass" and is not valid as the data part
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

I tried to export the S3 sdreport class from TMB using

#' @importClassesFrom TMB sdreport

and I got the following warning

1: class "sdreport" is not exported by 'namespace:TMB'

I am wondering if anyone else is having this problem and has a solution? I am honestly not sure how to export an S3 class to know if there is something that can be changed in TMB to allow the sdreport class to be exported as well as the sdreport() function. To replicate this error on your own machine you can clone https://github.com/NOAA-FIMS/FIMS, checkout dev and run the following code:

library(devtools)
withr::local_options(pkg.build_extra_flags = FALSE)
load_all()
devtools::document()

Thank you,
Kelli

messages.subject: Re: sdreport S3 class in TMB
messages.body_plain:
I don't use 'devtools', but I'm guessing that there is a bug in its
dependency 'pkgload'.  Debugging a bit suggests that the bug is in
pkgload::sort_s4classes, which is telling pkgload::remove_s4_classes to
remove your class definition for 'sdreport' before removing your class
definition for superclass 'sdreportOrList', when it is intended that
superclasses are removed first.

This happens when you run devtools::load_all() twice in a new R process.
The second load tries very hard to clean up after the first, and it
seems that you've hit an edge case where the "cleaning up" breaks
things.  The whole thing seems pretty dubious, relying on
methods::removeClass, where help("removeClass") says that it "can't be
used if the class is in another package" (and here pkgload != FIMS ...).

You should report to the 'pkgload' bug tracker.  Try
bug.report(package = "pkgload").   Ideally, you would include code that
is necessary and sufficient to reproduce the problem.  Maybe a trivial
package.tar.gz with R/test.R containing

     setOldClass("sdreport")

     setClassUnion("sdreportOrList", members = c("sdreport", "list"))

will be enough, but I haven't tested.

Mikael

Converting advector to double is made difficult on purpose, because it implicitly drops derivative tracking.
There is no exported function to do it, but one can use RTMB:::getValues.

Note that Ben's 'fixtmb' hack is not guarantied to work, as it relies on the internal AD storage in the special case where the advector is constant.
